patients.summary: Retired postal worker with ESRD from hypertensive nephrosclerosis, a failed 2016 kidney graft and a December 2020 re-transplant, and bipolar I disorder on lithium. His transplant course brings lithium nephrogenic DI, tacrolimus toxicity, acute and later chronic rejection, and three opportunistic infections (Pneumocystis, nocardiosis, cryptococcal meningitis).

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records packet from patient's previous primary care office, 41 pages, covering 2012 to 2019.

Highlights pulled by MA for PCP review:
- Hypertension for many years; kidney failure attributed to hypertensive nephrosclerosis, hemodialysis, then deceased-donor kidney transplant 2016.
- 2017: rejection episode treated by the transplant center with high-dose cyclophosphamide; complicated by hemorrhagic cystitis (gross hematuria, suprapubic pain), managed with IV hydration and mesna; finished the drug without further bladder trouble.
- 2019: transplant note copy, graft failed, back on in-center hemodialysis since March.
- Bipolar disorder type I on lithium since 2011, managed by his psychiatrist.
- Screening colonoscopy 2017 for transplant listing: normal to the terminal ileum, no polyps, 10-year interval.
- Hepatitis C antibody and HIV screen negative 2017 (listing labs).
- Tdap 2017.
- No known drug allergies.

Filed to chart.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
54 y/o man transferring primary care. Non-dialysis day. Sharp historian, has a typed medication list.

Kidneys: long-standing HTN -> ESRD (hypertensive nephrosclerosis), HD, then deceased-donor transplant 2016. Several rejections with that graft; the 2017 one needed high-dose cyclophosphamide and he developed hemorrhagic cystitis, treated with hydration and mesna, no bladder problems since. Graft failed early this year and he is back on in-center HD M/W/F through a L forearm fistula. Relisted at the transplant center. Transplant kept him on prednisone 5 mg; tacrolimus and mycophenolate were stopped when the graft failed.

Psych: bipolar I, on lithium since 2011, no admissions in years. His psychiatrist adjusted lithium for dialysis: one 300 mg capsule after each run, levels drawn at the unit.

Other: HTN on amlodipine. Former smoker, quit 2016. No alcohol. Retired from the postal service. Married. Fishes most mornings he is not at dialysis; used to fish bass tournaments when younger.

Family: father HTN and CKD. Sister bipolar disorder. Maternal uncle ESRD.

Meds: prednisone 5 daily, lithium 300 mg after HD, amlodipine 10 daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 138/86. Well appearing. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed RLQ transplant incision, nontender. L forearm AV fistula with good thrill. No edema. Neuro nonfocal. Mood euthymic, linear.

PHQ-9: 3.

A/P
1. ESRD on HD, failed 2016 graft, relisted: dialysis unit draws monthly labs; asked them to copy us. Transplant center remains lead for immunosuppression.
2. HTN: acceptable on amlodipine for a dialysis patient, unit tracks pre/post pressures.
3. Bipolar I, stable: lithium per psychiatry. Will request his psychiatrist's notes.
4. Hx cyclophosphamide hemorrhagic cystitis, resolved.
5. Health maintenance: colonoscopy 2017 normal (due 2027). Tdap 2017. Flu shot next month; no live vaccines.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Dialysis unit quarterly summary
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outpatient hemodialysis unit, quarterly care plan summary.

Patient: Ousmane Diallo. Modality: in-center hemodialysis three times weekly, 4 hours. Access: left forearm AV fistula, functioning well, no interventions this quarter.
Adequacy at goal. Interdialytic weight gains modest. Pre-dialysis BP generally 130s-140s systolic on amlodipine.
Monthly labs reviewed with the patient and acceptable for dialysis; no changes to his dialysis prescription.
Active on the deceased-donor transplant wait list.
Allergies: NKDA.
Copy to primary care per patient request.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Three month follow-up. Dialysis going smoothly, a bit tired the afternoons after runs, otherwise fine. No calls from transplant yet. Mood steady. Out on the river less now that it is cold.
Meds unchanged: prednisone 5, lithium 300 after HD, amlodipine 10.

O: Vitals as charted. Lungs clear, no edema, fistula thrill present.

A/P:
- ESRD on HD awaiting transplant: dialysis unit summary reviewed. Nothing to change.
- HTN: fine for a dialysis patient.
- Bipolar I: stable.
- Old cyclophosphamide cystitis: no urinary symptoms since 2017; marked resolved on the problem list.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Outpatient psychiatry annual letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outside psychiatry practice, annual update to primary care.

Mr. Diallo has bipolar I disorder, euthymic for many years on lithium. Since resuming hemodialysis he takes lithium carbonate 300 mg after each session; the dialysis unit draws a pre-dialysis level every month and his levels have stayed in the range we want. No mood episodes, sleeping well, no psychotic symptoms. Wife reports no concerns.

Plan: continue same dosing; when he receives a kidney he should call us so we can return him to twice-daily dosing with closer levels.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Transplant center discharge summary
documents.author: transplant surgery
documents.body:
Academic transplant center, inpatient transplant surgery service.
Admitted 12/03/2020. Discharged 12/10/2020.

Procedure: deceased-donor kidney transplant (second graft), 12/03/2020. First graft (2016) left in situ.
Indication: ESRD from hypertensive nephrosclerosis; failure of first graft after rejection episodes, on hemodialysis since 03/2019.

Course: immediate graft function, no dialysis needed after surgery. Creatinine fell steadily, 1.4 on the morning of discharge. Steroid taper started; prednisone to return to 5 mg daily per the taper calendar given to the patient. Psychiatry consulted for lithium now that he has a working kidney: back to 300 mg twice daily with a level in one week.

Discharge medications:
- tacrolimus 5 mg twice daily (levels at clinic)
- mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg twice daily
- prednisone per taper, then 5 mg daily
- trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole single strength daily (Pneumocystis prophylaxis)
- valganciclovir 450 mg daily for 6 months (CMV prophylaxis)
- lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily
- amlodipine 10 mg daily

Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: transplant clinic twice weekly for the first month. Hemodialysis discontinued; dialysis unit notified.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit: After Kidney Transplant
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, patient at home, wife present. Got his second kidney 12/3, home 12/10. Making plenty of urine, says it is strange not going to dialysis. Incision healing, a little sore. No fever. Transplant clinic twice a week, labs good so far per patient.

Med reconciliation from the discharge summary: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone taper down to 5 mg, TMP-SMX SS daily, valganciclovir 450 daily x 6 months, lithium back to 300 mg BID (psychiatry following the level), amlodipine 10 daily. Our list updated.

A/P: s/p deceased-donor re-transplant, early course smooth. Transplant team manages immunosuppression and labs. Talked about avoiding NSAIDs and checking with us/transplant before any new medicine. Will see in person in a few months; COVID vaccine as soon as he is eligible.
